title: LLMs: A Driving Force in Next Generation Digital Design Automation
problem: Silicon design automation faces growing complexity and scale; current approaches lack effective methods to leverage generative AI for automating diverse design tasks.
motivation: LLMs show transformative potential in automating labor-intensive silicon design processes; exploring their capabilities and readiness is critical for advancing design automation.
method: This is a review paper surveying how large language models—AI systems trained on vast amounts of text—can help automate silicon chip design. The authors review existing applications, evaluate which chip design tasks LLMs are ready to tackle, and identify research gaps that must be closed to expand their use.
key_novelty: The paper systematically maps where large language models can be applied to chip design automation tasks, evaluates their readiness for practical use, and identifies remaining research gaps.
contributions: Comprehensive review of LLM applications in silicon design automation
Qualitative analysis of technology readiness for various design tasks
Identification of research directions for LLM-driven design automation
Discussion of transformative potential of generative AI in chip design
limitations: Position paper without empirical results; specific quantitative comparisons and benchmarks not provided.
primary_theme: LLMs as transformative agents in silicon design automation
